title: PF4 drives mechanical overload-induced temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis through TLR2-dependent activation of NF-kappaB.
authors: Sun, Wei; Wu, Jiashun; Liu, Yu; Li, Xiang; Zeng, Guozhong; Li, Kan; Su, Kai; Xia, Juan; Zheng, Guangsen
one_liner_zh: 该文研究PF4通过TLR2激活NF-kappaB通路在颞下颌关节骨关节炎中的作用，属于纯湿实验与信号通路机制研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mechanical overload‑related cytokines contribute to temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJOA) pathogenesis. This study investigated the role of overload‑associated platelet factor 4 (PF4). METHODS: Combined proteomic screening of human TMJOA synovial fluid (SF) and finite element simulation identified mechanically linked cytokines. A rat unilateral anterior crossbite (UAC) model was used to induce TMJ cartilage degeneration. To dissect the mechanism, primary rat TMJ chondrocytes were treated with PF4 and analyzed by transcriptomics and functional assays. Further, specific inhibitors targeting the canonical nuclear factor‑kappaB (NF-kappaB) pathway (TPCA-1) or TLR2 (C29) were applied in vitro to pinpoint the signaling cascade. Their potential therapeutic effects were further assessed by administration in the UAC model. RESULTS: Clinical samples revealed elevated PF4 levels in the SF of TMJOA patients, correlating with simulated mechanical stress at the condyle. In a rat UAC model, mechanical overload similarly upregulated PF4 in TMJ, concomitant with cartilage degeneration, anabolic-catabolic imbalance, and cellular senescence. In vitro, PF4 stimulation of primary chondrocytes suppressed anabolic markers while upregulating catabolic factors and senescence markers. Mechanistically, PF4 uniquely activated the canonical NF-kappaB pathway by directly engaging surface TLR2, bypassing its classical chemokine receptor C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (CXCR3). This PF4-TLR2 interaction was both necessary and sufficient for downstream NF-kappaB-driven gene dysregulation. Notably, this PF4-TLR2 axis upregulates B-cell CLL/lymphoma 3 (BCL3), which in turn promotes pathway activation by accelerating early phosphorylation of p65, revealing an intrinsic feedback loop that fine-tunes the inflammatory response. In vivo, inhibition of TLR2 or canonical NF-kappaB signaling in the UAC model significantly mitigated overload-induced cartilage dysregulation and subchondral bone damage. CONCLUSION: We delineate a novel mechanotransduction pathway in TMJOA, where overload-induced PF4 acts as an alarmin that signals through TLR2 to activate the canonical NF-kappaB cascade, a process further amplified by the downstream regulator BCL3, ultimately disrupting cartilage homeostasis. This work establishes the PF4-TLR2-NF-kappaB axis as a crucial pathogenic driver and a promising therapeutic target for load-related TMJ degeneration.
abstract_zh: 背景：机械过载相关细胞因子参与颞下颌关节骨关节炎（TMJOA）的发病机制。本研究探讨了过载相关血小板因子4（PF4）的作用。方法：结合人TMJOA滑液（SF）的蛋白质组学筛选和有限元模拟，识别出机械相关细胞因子。采用大鼠单侧前牙反颌（UAC）模型诱导TMJ软骨退变。为解析机制，用PF4处理大鼠原代TMJ软骨细胞，并通过转录组学和功能实验进行分析。进一步，在体外应用靶向经典核因子-κB（NF-kappaB）通路（TPCA-1）或TLR2（C29）的特异性抑制剂，以明确信号级联反应。在UAC模型中给药，进一步评估其潜在治疗效果。结果：临床样本显示，TMJOA患者滑液中PF4水平升高，与髁突模拟机械应力相关。在大鼠UAC模型中，机械过载同样上调TMJ中的PF4，伴随软骨退变、合成-分解代谢失衡和细胞衰老。体外实验中，PF4刺激原代软骨细胞抑制合成代谢标志物，同时上调分解代谢因子和衰老标志物。机制上，PF4通过直接结合表面TLR2，绕过其经典趋化因子受体C-X-C基序趋化因子受体3（CXCR3），独特地激活经典NF-kappaB通路。这种PF4-TLR2相互作用对下游NF-kappaB驱动的基因失调既是必要的也是充分的。值得注意的是，该PF4-TLR2轴上调B细胞CLL/淋巴瘤3（BCL3），后者通过加速p65的早期磷酸化促进通路激活，揭示了一个微调炎症反应的内在反馈环路。在体内，UAC模型中抑制TLR2或经典NF-kappaB信号显著减轻了过载诱导的软骨失调和软骨下骨损伤。结论：我们描绘了TMJOA中一条新的机械转导通路，其中过载诱导的PF4作为警报素，通过TLR2信号激活经典NF-kappaB级联反应，该过程被下游调节因子BCL3进一步放大，最终破坏软骨稳态。本研究确立了PF4-TLR2-NF-kappaB轴作为负荷相关TMJ退变的关键致病驱动因素和有前景的治疗靶点。
